sources.title: CLM schema
sources.summary: Context followed by question is encoded as prose; each choice description is an independently encoded action. Confidence is top probability minus mean remainder, not calibrated success probability.

sources.title: CLM release
sources.summary: Default 2048-token truncation requires a client budget guard. Reported 81.6% DeepSWE is 31/38 held-out tasks with best-of-N verification, not the full benchmark or one-pass coding. Encoder, head and pooling must match.

sources.title: HarnessTax
sources.summary: 21 pairs; 30 tasks per benchmark; three attempts; native high settings; 100-turn cap. Costs recomputed at fixed API rates, not measured subscription consumption. Alternative harnesses lead in 9/12 eligible comparisons, not all workloads. Native effort semantics differ.

sources.title: ARC Prize Astra evaluation
sources.summary: ARC-AGI-3 semi-private: standard harness Astra max 62.7%/$26098; provider adapter high 99.9%/$18817. The adapter preserves reasoning state. Different settings and game tasks preclude a pure coding comparison. Useful evidence against a universal less-scaffolding-is-better rule.

sources.title: Codex plan usage
sources.summary: Allowance use depends on model, task location, complexity, context, reasoning, speed and tools. Check /status and actual plan dashboard. Do not convert API dollars directly into quota percentages.

sources.title: Codex authentication
sources.summary: Native ChatGPT sign-in uses subscription access; API-key authentication is separately usage-billed. This page does not establish that every third-party OAuth implementation is a permitted subscription transport.

sources.title: Claude Code authentication boundary
sources.summary: End users may sign into the unmodified Claude Code binary using their own subscription. Third-party credential collection/intermediation and offering Claude.ai sign-in in another application are restricted. Use native worker delegation, not extracted subscription tokens.

sources.title: Claude Code cost and cache observations
sources.summary: Native cost/cache reports distinguish input, cache writes and reads. Version-specific statistics require capability discovery; displayed API-equivalent cost is not a calibrated subscription-depletion measure.

sources.title: Astra capabilities
sources.summary: gpt-6-astra supports low, medium, high, xhigh and max. AgenticArch deliberately exposes high only; provider support is not permission to widen the menu.

sources.title: Luna capabilities
sources.summary: gpt-6-luna supports several efforts. AgenticArch permits low/high only. The documented medium default must be overridden explicitly.

sources.title: Astra launch
sources.summary: Reported maxima: DeepSWE 1.1 Astra 74.1%, Fable5.1 67.4%; Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 Astra64.6%, Fable5.1 52.6%. Results use research/API environments and are not direct GPT-6 Pro web or uniformly high-effort measurements.

sources.title: Sol and Luna launch
sources.summary: DeepSWE1.1 Luna max 66.6%. The launch establishes a price/performance trade-off, not the locally optimal high-effort quota setting. The supplied chart is a hypothesis input, not a machine-readable measured effort sweep.

sources.title: Opus5.5 identity and effort
sources.summary: claude-opus-5-5; released 2026-09-22; default medium, adaptive thinking always on. Model- and conversation-bound thinking blocks require careful handoffs; actual client mappings still need local verification.

sources.title: Fable5.1 identity and effort
sources.summary: claude-fable-5-1; default high. Per-message effort support is not proof that a particular Claude Code bridge exposes it. Fable5.5 has no verified activation evidence in this review.

sources.title: Opus5.5 evaluation
sources.summary: Opus5.5 medium: FrontierCode1.1 Main54.6%, CursorBench4.0 52.5%. Terminal-Bench4.0: Opus xhigh66.4%, Astra high57.9%, Fable5.1 55.8%. Other table entries generally use max. Some Claude tests use fallback models after safeguard interventions; scores are not pure single-model results. Science margins have standard errors of 3.5–5 points. Do not compare Main with Extended.

sources.title: Sonar Opus5.5 evaluation
sources.summary: Prasenjit Sarkar, 2026-09-22. Java, Opus5.5 high versus Opus5 Thinking. 4444 generated tasks; executable pass rate covers544 HumanEval/MBPP tasks:87.68% versus88.6%. Less output and fewer total findings, but bug density rises12% and concurrency findings44%. Static findings are not proven runtime incidents; no Astra/Pro/Fable5.1 head-to-head.

sources.title: Astra visual effort sweep
sources.summary: Simon Willison, 2026-09-04. Published SVG artifacts across efforts show visual gains over earlier GPT5.6 models and remaining geometry errors. One creative prompt is not a broad frontend benchmark; comparison Luna is GPT5.6, not GPT6.

sources.title: Fable5.1 visual experiment
sources.summary: Simon Willison, 2026-09-01. Published visual outputs and effort traces support hands-on creative testing, not a reliable Fable-versus-Opus5.5 frontend advantage.

sources.title: Harness overhead experiment
sources.summary: Josh Owens distinguishes startup/config overhead from long-run transcript replay. His small-call dollar reduction did not transfer to a long research run dominated by cached replay. Single-user experiment, not a controlled quota study.

sources.title: Astra-Ares checkpoint design
sources.summary: Effort is applied before generation through native settings with an acknowledgement; leases count generations, not tool calls. Native prefix fixtures do not establish workload savings or long-session compaction support.

sources.title: Pi extension controls
sources.summary: setModel and setThinkingLevel exist; thinking level may be clamped. Extensions share process permissions. Effective runtime and provider mapping require verification; an OAuth provider declaration is not subscription authorization.

excluded_claims: Universal zero quality loss from Pi
API dollar savings equal quota savings
All backend work favors Pro empirically
All frontend work favors Opus5.5 empirically
CLM best-of-N is single-pass full-benchmark performance
limits: No controlled current-model, two-harness subscription-quota study was located. New-model first-hand comparative editorial coverage is sparse. No source is promoted to local qualification automatically.
